Condition Trend Over Time

Deadstock items command a $321.67 margin premium over Used and $226.38 over VNDS. Only 0.0% of Used-condition sales clear retail, compared to 100.0% for Deadstock. The resale-to-retail ratio for Deadstock is 2.38x, while Used drops to 0.70x — well below break-even on average. VNDS occupies a middle ground with a 1.20x ratio and 83.3% premium rate.
VNDS margins are substantially closer to Used than to Deadstock — the condition premium is not linear. Sourcing strategies that assume VNDS will capture most of the Deadstock premium will overestimate returns.

Channel Performance by Condition

Margin performance varies by condition across channels — some platforms may be better suited for Deadstock inventory while others compensate with velocity on Used product.

Inventory Velocity Distribution

Beyond averages, the distribution of days-in-inventory reveals how consistently each channel turns over stock. Tighter boxes indicate more predictable velocity.

Walk-in Retail delivers the highest average margin at $89.55, while StockX offers the fastest inventory turnover at 8 days average. The margin–velocity tradeoff is the central channel decision: a seller holding Deadstock inventory of a high-demand colorway may prefer the premium channel despite longer hold times, while a seller moving Used product should prioritize velocity to minimize holding costs and depreciation risk.

6. Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

Key Findings

  1. Condition is the dominant pricing driver. Deadstock commands a $321.67 margin premium over Used. The probability of selling above retail drops from 100.0% (Deadstock) to 0.0% (Used). Maintaining Deadstock condition through the resale cycle is the single highest-impact lever for profitability.
  2. Colorway selection outweighs model selection. While Air Jordan 11 Retro leads on model-level margin, the spread between the best and worst colorways within any given model exceeds the spread between models. The top model–colorway combos (e.g., Air Jordan 11 Retro — Pine Green at $134.16) dramatically outperform the model average, confirming that colorway is the sharper sourcing filter.
  3. Margin and velocity are inversely correlated across channels. Walk-in Retail offers the highest margins but not the fastest turnover, while StockX moves product quickest. The optimal channel depends on inventory condition and holding-cost tolerance.
  4. A majority of transactions do not clear retail. With an overall premium rate of 61.3%, more than 38.7% of transactions sell below MSRP. Profitability is concentrated in specific model–colorway–condition combinations rather than being a market-wide phenomenon.
  5. VNDS does not capture most of the Deadstock premium. The VNDS-to-Deadstock margin gap ($226.38) is 0.7x the VNDS-to-Used gap ($95.28). Condition depreciation is front-loaded — even slight wear significantly erodes value.

Strategic Recommendations

  1. Prioritize Deadstock sourcing for high-margin colorways. Focus procurement on Deadstock inventory of Pine Green, and the top 3–5 colorways by margin. The premium rate for Deadstock (100.0%) means the probability of a profitable sale is materially higher, justifying higher acquisition cost.
  2. Match channel to inventory condition. List Deadstock and high-margin VNDS on Walk-in Retail for maximum price realization. Route Used-condition inventory to StockX or other fast-turnover channels to minimize holding costs and reduce exposure to further depreciation.
  3. Cap inventory hold times at 34 days for non-Deadstock. Used-condition product depreciates with time. Set a maximum holding period 50% above the market average; if a Used shoe hasn't sold within that window, consider markdown or channel switch to accelerate exit.
  4. Time listings around high-margin months. Listing concentration around seasonally strong periods (such as 05/2025) can improve average clearing prices. Monitor quarterly margin trends and adjust listing cadence accordingly.
  5. Build a model–colorway margin matrix for sourcing decisions. Use the model–colorway cross-analysis as a sourcing scorecard. Rank combinations by both margin and velocity, and set acquisition price ceilings based on the target resale-to-retail ratio. Avoid sourcing low-ratio colorways (below 1.0x) unless acquisition cost is significantly below retail.
Data limitation: This analysis is based on 5,000 synthetically generated transactions modeling realistic market behavior. While directional insights are valid, exact margin figures and seasonal patterns should be validated against live marketplace data before committing capital. The synthetic nature may underrepresent extreme market events (hype drops, collaboration releases) that can produce outsized premiums.
